spear.text: The cheapest defender and the backbone of any garrison. Its strength is holding off cavalry, so a village full of spearmen makes raiders on horseback think twice. On the attack it is weak; keep it at home.

sword.text: A sturdy defender against infantry and archers, slower than the spearman and heavier on iron. Pair the two and a village stands against almost any mix of attackers.

axe.text: The infantry that attacks. It hits hard for its price but barely defends, so send axemen out and keep other troops at home. Most early conquests are won with a wall of axes.

archer.text: A defender that shines against cavalry and infantry alike but falls quickly to mounted archers. It costs more wood than the other foot soldiers and pays for it on the wall.

scout.text: Scouts sneak into a village and report what they saw: troops, buildings and resources. They do not fight, and scouts at home are the only thing that stops enemy scouts. Send a few before every big attack.

lightCav.text: Fast, strong in attack and able to carry a lot, the light cavalryman is the raider of choice. It dies quickly against spearmen, so scout first and pick villages that have none.

mountedArcher.text: A rider who shoots: strong in attack and hard for archers to stop. It is costly and needs a well-built Stable and Smithy, so it comes later in a village's life.

heavyCav.text: Expensive and strong at everything. Heavy cavalry defends as well as it attacks, which makes it a good answer when a neighbour comes at you from several sides.

ram.text: Rams do not fight; they knock down the wall so the rest of the army can. Send them with a strong force, because a ram that arrives alone achieves nothing.

catapult.text: Catapults damage the building you aim them at, from the farm to the Town Hall. They are slow and need an escort, but they can take a rival village apart level by level.

paladin.text: One knight per village, raised at the Pedestal. It defends very well, above all against cavalry, and makes a strong escort for an important attack.

noble.text: The hetman is how villages change hands. Every hetman that survives a won attack lowers the village's loyalty, and at zero the village is yours. It needs coins minted in the Academy and cannot march too far.

main.text: The heart of the village. Every level makes all other building work faster, and many buildings need a certain Town Hall level first. Raise it early and keep raising it.

barracks.text: Where infantry is trained: spearmen, swordsmen, axemen and archers. Higher levels train them faster, which matters when you need a garrison in a hurry.

stable.text: Trains scouts and every kind of cavalry. It needs the Barracks and the Smithy first; once it stands, raiding becomes much faster.

workshop.text: Builds rams and catapults, the siege engines that break walls and buildings. It comes later, after a well-grown Town Hall and Smithy.

academy.text: Mints the coins that pay for hetmans and trains the hetmans themselves. It needs Town Hall 20, Market 10 and Smithy 20, so it is the mark of a grown village.

smithy.text: The Smithy opens the way to better troops: most units need a certain Smithy level before they can be trained. Plan its levels together with the army you want.

statue.text: The Pedestal raises the knight, one per village. It has a single level and asks for little, so build it once your village has room.

market.text: Merchants leave from here to carry resources to another village, yours or a neighbour's. Send a surplus where it is short and no resource has to wait for another.

wood.text: Produces wood, the resource almost everything needs. Its production grows with every level, so the first hours are mostly about the three resource buildings.

clay.text: Produces clay for buildings and troops. Keep it close to the Lumber Mill in level, or clay will be the thing you always wait for.

iron.text: Produces iron, which weighs most in the price of good troops. A village that plans to attack needs a strong Ironworks.

farm.text: Every building and every unit needs people, and the Farmstead sets how many the village can feed. When it is full, nothing new can be built or trained.

storage.text: Sets how much of each resource the village can hold. Production beyond it is lost, so raise it before long trips away from the game.

hide.text: The Hideout keeps part of your resources where raiders cannot take them. It does not stop an attack, but it makes your village a poor target for looting.

wall.text: The wall makes every defender in the village stronger. Rams can lower it, which is why attackers bring them, and why a good wall is worth rebuilding quickly.
